explanation_en: This expression means to clarify something beyond doubt or to make it very obvious. The word 'bem' functions as an intensifier meaning 'very' or 'well'. It is an essential phrase for structuring arguments and avoiding misunderstandings in conversation.

examples.en_text: I want to make it very clear that I don't agree with this decision.
examples.target_text: Eu quero deixar bem claro que não concordo com essa decisão.

examples.en_text: The boss made it very clear that the deadline is Friday.
examples.target_text: O chefe deixou bem claro que o prazo final é sexta-feira.

examples.en_text: I hope she makes it very clear what she really wants.
examples.target_text: Espero que ela deixe bem claro o que realmente quer.

examples.en_text: They made it very clear that they won't accept late projects.
examples.target_text: Eles deixaram bem claro que não vão aceitar projetos atrasados.

examples.en_text: She made it very clear to him that they are just friends.
examples.target_text: Ela deixou bem claro para ele que eles são apenas amigos.

examples.en_text: It is important to make it very clear what the rules of the game are.
examples.target_text: É importante deixar bem claro quais são as regras do jogo.

explanation_en: This expression refers to the feeling of embarrassment or cringe you experience on behalf of someone else who is doing something awkward or foolish. It is a very common concept in modern Brazilian culture and social media. Note that 'alheia' is an adjective meaning 'belonging to others', so it literally translates to 'others' embarrassment'.

examples.en_text: I had to turn off the television because that scene gave me a lot of secondhand embarrassment.
examples.target_text: Eu tive que desligar a televisão porque aquela cena me deu muita vergonha alheia.

examples.en_text: That comedy show is full of secondhand embarrassments that I can barely watch.
examples.target_text: Aquele programa de comédia é cheio de vergonhas alheias que eu mal consigo assistir.

examples.en_text: I feel a huge secondhand embarrassment when I see someone going through that situation on the street.
examples.target_text: Eu sinto uma vergonha alheia enorme quando vejo alguém passando por essa situação na rua.

examples.en_text: I avoid watching these videos on the internet to save my heart from so many secondhand embarrassments.
examples.target_text: Evito ver esses vídeos na internet para poupar o meu coração de tantas vergonhas alheias.

examples.en_text: He tried to tell a joke in the middle of the meeting, but only caused secondhand embarrassment to everyone.
examples.target_text: Ele tentou contar uma piada no meio da reunião, mas só causou vergonha alheia em todo mundo.

examples.en_text: I don't like reality shows because they are full of secondhand embarrassments from beginning to end.
examples.target_text: Não gosto de reality shows porque eles estão cheios de vergonhas alheias do início ao fim.

explanation_en: This expression means to feel pity, sympathy, or compassion for someone. 'Dó' is a masculine noun, so you say 'ter dó de alguém' or 'ficar com dó de'. It is highly common in everyday spoken Portuguese and carries a slightly more colloquial, warm tone than 'ter pena'.

examples.en_text: I feel sorry for that stray dog, he looks so skinny and hungry.
examples.target_text: Eu tenho dó daquele cachorro de rua, ele parece tão magro e faminto.

examples.en_text: At first, the neighbors felt sorry for him, but then they realized he didn't want to work.
examples.target_text: No início, os vizinhos tinham dó dele, mas depois perceberam que ele não queria trabalhar.

examples.en_text: Please, have mercy on me and don't tell me the ending of the movie!
examples.target_text: Por favor, tenha dó de mim e não me conte o final do filme!

examples.en_text: It's hard not to feel sorry for the people who lost everything in the flood.
examples.target_text: É difícil não ter dó das pessoas que perderam tudo na enchente.

examples.en_text: We felt sorry for the secretary because she had to work late on her birthday.
examples.target_text: Nós tivemos dó da secretária porque ela teve que trabalhar até tarde no aniversário dela.

examples.en_text: That boss has no pity on anyone; he demands that everyone work overtime without complaining.
examples.target_text: Aquele chefe não tem dó de ninguém; ele exige que todos façam horas extras sem reclamar.

explanation_en: This is a fixed idiomatic formula used exactly like the English 'believe it or not' to introduce or conclude a statement that is highly surprising or hard to believe. It uses the imperative form of 'acreditar' followed by the future subjunctive of 'querer'. It can be placed at the beginning, middle, or end of a sentence.

examples.en_text: Believe it or not, I finally learned how to cook this year.
examples.target_text: Acredite se quiser, eu finalmente aprendi a cozinhar este ano.

examples.en_text: Believe it or not, we met by chance in the middle of Paris.
examples.target_text: Acredite se quiser, nós nos encontramos por acaso no meio de Paris.

examples.en_text: Believe it or not, but it hasn't rained at all this month.
examples.target_text: Acredite se quiser, mas ainda não choveu nada este mês.

examples.en_text: Believe it or not, he started working at the company as an intern and today he is the director.
examples.target_text: Acredite se quiser, ele começou a trabalhar na empresa como estagiário e hoje é o diretor.

examples.en_text: She lives in Rio de Janeiro but, believe it or not, she hates going to the beach.
examples.target_text: Ela mora no Rio de Janeiro mas, acredite se quiser, ela detesta ir à praia.

examples.en_text: Believe it or not, this old watch cost only ten euros at a flea market.
examples.target_text: Acredite se quiser, este relógio antigo custou apenas dez euros em uma feira.

explanation_en: A very common colloquial expression meaning to annoy, irritate, or pester someone. While highly informal and slightly edgy, it is widely used in daily life and is not considered highly vulgar. You can use it transitively as 'encher o saco de alguém' or simply as an exclamation of annoyance.

examples.en_text: My boss has been bugging me all day about this report.
examples.target_text: O meu chefe está o dia todo enchendo o meu saco com esse relatório.

examples.en_text: Stop talking about that! You're already annoying me.
examples.target_text: Para de falar disso! Você já está enchendo o meu saco.

examples.en_text: These unknown numbers keep calling me and bugging me.
examples.target_text: Esses números desconhecidos ficam me ligando e enchendo o meu saco.

examples.en_text: He keeps bugging me to go to the party with him.
examples.target_text: Ele continua enchendo o meu saco para eu ir à festa com ele.

examples.en_text: The cat is annoying me because it wants food right now.
examples.target_text: O gato está enchendo o meu saco porque quer comida agora.

examples.en_text: That construction noise has been bugging me since early this morning.
examples.target_text: Aquele barulho da obra está enchendo o meu saco desde cedo.

explanation_en: A fixed grammatical construction used to express absolute determination, meaning 'no matter the cost' or 'whatever it takes'. It uses the present subjunctive of 'custar' in the first part and the future subjunctive in the second part. It is common in both spoken and written registers.

examples.en_text: We have to deliver this project by Friday, whatever it takes.
examples.target_text: Temos que entregar este projeto até sexta-feira, custe o que custar.

examples.en_text: I am going to pass my driving test, whatever it takes.
examples.target_text: Eu vou conseguir passar no exame de condução, custe o que custar.

examples.en_text: She promised to protect her family, at all costs.
examples.target_text: Ela prometeu proteger a sua família, custe o que custar.

examples.en_text: This year we are going on vacation to Japan, whatever it takes.
examples.target_text: Este ano nós vamos de férias para o Japão, custe o que custar.

examples.en_text: They want to buy that house, at all costs.
examples.target_text: Eles querem comprar aquela casa, custe o que custar.

examples.en_text: I will find out the truth, whatever it takes.
examples.target_text: Eu vou descobrir a verdade, custe o que custar.

explanation_en: While the verb 'rir' means to laugh, native Portuguese speakers very frequently use the collocation 'dar risada' in casual speech. It sounds highly natural and can imply a continuous or lighthearted act of laughing rather than a single sudden laugh.

examples.en_text: Whenever I told that joke, my grandfather used to laugh.
examples.target_text: Sempre que eu contava aquela piada, meu avô dava risada.

examples.en_text: The children laughed at their uncle's antics at the party.
examples.target_text: As crianças davam risada das palhaçadas do tio na festa.

examples.en_text: We used to laugh at any silly thing when we were teenagers.
examples.target_text: Nós dávamos risada de qualquer bobagem quando éramos adolescentes.

examples.en_text: I laughed when I saw the old photo you sent me.
examples.target_text: Eu dei risada quando vi a foto antiga que você me mandou.

examples.en_text: She couldn't stand the silence in the middle of the meeting and laughed.
examples.target_text: Ela não aguentou o silêncio no meio da reunião e deu risada.

examples.en_text: He was a serious man, but he used to laugh at comedy movies.
examples.target_text: Ele era um homem sério, mas dava risada com os filmes de comédia.

explanation_en: This idiomatic phrase is used to refer to a known, often negative or chaotic, outcome of a series of events. It carries a tone of 'and we all know how that turned out' or 'look at the mess it caused'. It is highly colloquial and common in spoken Brazilian Portuguese.

examples.en_text: They spent more than they could on their credit card and look what happened: now they are deep in debt.
examples.target_text: Eles gastaram mais do que podiam no cartão de crédito e deu no que deu: agora estão cheios de dívidas.

examples.en_text: We didn't talk about the problem at the time and we saw how that turned out, we ended up having a huge fight.
examples.target_text: Nós não conversamos sobre o problema na época e deu no que deu, acabamos brigando feio.

examples.en_text: He decided to do the report at the last minute and look what happened, the boss didn't like the result.
examples.target_text: Ele decidiu fazer o relatório de última hora e deu no que deu, o chefe não gostou do resultado.

examples.en_text: I warned him to take a coat, but he didn't listen to me and look what happened: he caught a cold.
examples.target_text: Eu avisei para ele levar um casaco, mas ele não me ouviu e deu no que deu: pegou um resfriado.

examples.en_text: She tried to fix the washing machine by herself and look what happened, now the kitchen floor is flooded.
examples.target_text: Ela tentou consertar a máquina de lavar sozinha e deu no que deu, agora o chão da cozinha está inundado.

examples.en_text: We took a shortcut without knowing the way and we saw how that turned out, we were lost for two hours.
examples.target_text: Nós pegamos um atalho sem conhecer o caminho e deu no que deu, ficamos perdidos por duas horas.

explanation_en: An informal expression used to introduce an additional benefit or consequence that comes along with a main action. It translates well to 'as a bonus', 'into the bargain', or 'on top of that'. It is very common in casual conversation and promotional contexts.

examples.en_text: We traveled to Rio de Janeiro and, as a bonus, managed to see the sunset in Ipanema.
examples.target_text: Viajamos para o Rio de Janeiro e, de quebra, conseguimos ver o pôr do sol em Ipanema.

examples.en_text: He finished the report early and, on top of that, helped his colleagues with the project.
examples.target_text: Ele terminou o relatório mais cedo e, de quebra, ajudou os colegas com o projeto.

examples.en_text: I bought a new cell phone and got a case as a bonus.
examples.target_text: Comprei um celular novo e ganhei uma capinha de quebra.

examples.en_text: I started walking every day to lose weight and, as a bonus, improved my sleep.
examples.target_text: Comecei a caminhar todos os dias para emagrecer e, de quebra, melhorei meu sono.

examples.en_text: She prepared a wonderful dinner and, on top of that, made a delicious dessert.
examples.target_text: Ela preparou um jantar maravilhoso e, de quebra, fez uma sobremesa deliciosa.

examples.en_text: Taking this course helped me at work and, as a bonus, I met amazing people.
examples.target_text: Fazer esse curso me ajudou no trabalho e, de quebra, conheci pessoas incríveis.

explanation_en: Puxar o gancho is a very common conversational transition in Portuguese, meaning to connect one's next point to what was just said. It is widely used by journalists, podcast hosts, and in professional meetings to transition smoothly. It comes from the literal meaning of pulling a hook.

examples.en_text: I want to build on what Maria said to present our new proposal.
examples.target_text: Quero puxar o gancho do que a Maria disse para apresentar a nossa nova proposta.

examples.en_text: I'm going to use your last sentence as a hook and ask about the future of the project.
examples.target_text: Vou puxar o gancho da sua última frase e perguntar sobre o futuro do projeto.

examples.en_text: Building on the previous topic, I think we should schedule another meeting.
examples.target_text: Puxando o gancho do assunto anterior, acho que devíamos marcar outra reunião.

examples.en_text: To build on his presentation, I would like to show this chart.
examples.target_text: Para puxar o gancho da apresentação dele, gostaria de mostrar este gráfico.

examples.en_text: She built on our conversation from yesterday and solved the problem quickly.
examples.target_text: Ela puxou o gancho da nossa conversa de ontem e resolveu o problema rapidamente.

examples.en_text: We can use this idea as a hook to create a better marketing campaign.
examples.target_text: Podemos puxar o gancho dessa ideia para criar uma campanha de marketing melhor.

explanation_en: Treta is an extremely common colloquial word in Brazil. It can mean a fight, confusion, a lie, or a complicated situation. In political or social contexts, it refers to conflicts, controversies, or 'beef.'

examples.en_text: I prefer to mind my own business and not get involved in drama at work.
examples.target_text: Eu prefiro ficar na minha e não me envolver em tretas no trabalho.

examples.en_text: They are always arguing on the internet, it seems like they love drama.
examples.target_text: Eles estão sempre discutindo na internet, parece que adoram tretas.

examples.en_text: I don't care about their beef, I just want them to make up.
examples.target_text: Eu não quero saber das tretas deles, só quero que eles façam as pazes.

examples.en_text: Avoid that group of people, they only bring trouble and confusion.
examples.target_text: Evita aquele grupo de pessoas, eles só trazem tretas e confusão.

examples.en_text: Last Christmas, there was a big family drama over money.
examples.target_text: No Natal passado, houve uma grande treta na família por causa de dinheiro.

examples.en_text: Don't look for trouble with me today, because I'm not in the mood.
examples.target_text: Não procures tretas comigo hoje, porque não estou com paciência.

explanation_en: Se apoderar de means to take possession of something, often without permission or in a dominant way. It is a pronominal verb requiring the preposition 'de'. It is highly useful in political, legal, and everyday contexts to describe someone taking over a resource or power.

examples.en_text: Panic took over the crowd when the alarm started to ring.
examples.target_text: O pânico se apoderou da multidão quando o alarme começou a tocar.

examples.en_text: The new board of directors took over control of the company quickly.
examples.target_text: A nova diretoria se apoderou do controle da empresa de forma rápida.

examples.en_text: A deep silence took over the room after the sad news.
examples.target_text: Um silêncio profundo se apoderou da sala após a triste notícia.

examples.en_text: The rebel group took over the local radio station to broadcast their message.
examples.target_text: O grupo rebelde se apoderou da rádio local para transmitir sua mensagem.

examples.en_text: A great nostalgia took over him when looking at the old childhood photos.
examples.target_text: Uma grande nostalgia se apoderou dele ao rever as fotos antigas da infância.

examples.en_text: Tiredness took over me and I fell asleep right after dinner.
examples.target_text: O cansaço se apoderou de mim e eu dormi logo depois do jantar.
